wine-rack.definition: A frame or set of shelves designed to store wine bottles.
wine-rack.exampleUsage: The museum display showed bottles stored on a wine rack.

temperature-control.definition: Equipment or procedures used to maintain a chosen storage temperature.

humidity-control.definition: Equipment or procedures used to regulate moisture in the storage-room air.

stone-wall.definition: A wall built from stone that may support soil, enclose land, or mark the edge of a property.

cellar-door.definition: The door leading into a cellar or underground storage room.
cellar-door.exampleUsage: The cellar door was kept locked.

tasting-table.definition: A table set aside for organized sensory evaluation or comparison of food or beverages.
tasting-table.exampleUsage: The educational display used a tasting table for labeled samples.

dim-lighting.definition: Low illumination that does not by itself establish adequate visibility or safety.

ventilation.definition: The exchange of indoor air with fresh air, by natural or mechanical means.

insulation.definition: Material or construction that reduces heat transfer into or out of the cellar.

wine-fridge.definition: A refrigerator designed to store wine bottles at controlled temperatures.
wine-fridge.exampleUsage: The exhibit explains that a wine fridge controls storage temperature.

horizontal-storage.definition: A storage arrangement in which objects are kept lying flat or on their sides.
horizontal-storage.exampleUsage: The diagram shows horizontal storage for bottles.

bottle.definition: A glass or plastic vessel used for storing drinks or other liquids.

cork.definition: The plug in the mouth of a bottle (especially a wine bottle).

capsule.definition: A thin covering around the neck and top of a wine bottle.

label.definition: Printed identification information attached to a bottle or its packaging.

vintage.definition: The grape-harvest year identified for a wine under the relevant labeling rules.

bin-number.definition: A number used to identify a particular storage location, compartment, or group of items.
bin-number.exampleUsage: The cellar book records each bin number.

cellar-book.definition: A record used to track items stored in a cellar, such as bottle locations, dates, or inventory.
cellar-book.exampleUsage: The curator checked the cellar book for the recorded location.

inventory.definition: The stored stock of bottles or a record of that stock.

collection.definition: Several things grouped together or considered as a whole.

decanter.definition: A glass container used to serve wine after pouring it from a bottle.

wine-glass.definition: A stemmed drinking glass traditionally used for wine.
wine-glass.exampleUsage: The glassware display included an empty wine glass.

wine-opener.definition: A tool designed to remove a cork or other closure from a wine bottle.
wine-opener.exampleUsage: The display case contained several historical wine openers.

aerator.definition: A device that exposes wine to air while it is poured.

wine-stopper.definition: A reusable closure designed to seal an opened wine bottle.
wine-stopper.exampleUsage: The exhibit showed different types of wine stoppers.

wine-pourer.definition: A small fitting placed at a bottle opening to control the flow of liquid while pouring.
wine-pourer.exampleUsage: The equipment display included a bottle pourer.

champagne-flute.definition: A slender stemmed glass with a tall narrow bowl.
champagne-flute.exampleUsage: The glassware display places an empty Champagne flute beside a coupe.

ice-bucket.definition: An insulated container used to hold ice or keep a bottle cool.
ice-bucket.exampleUsage: The hotel display included a stainless-steel ice bucket.

wine-thermometer.definition: A thermometer designed to measure the temperature of wine or its storage environment.
wine-thermometer.exampleUsage: The museum exhibit shows a wine thermometer used for temperature monitoring.

bordeaux.definition: A wine-growing region around Bordeaux in southwestern France.

burgundy.definition: A region in eastern France associated with wine production.

champagne.definition: A wine-growing region in northeastern France, also associated with a protected sparkling-wine designation.
champagne.exampleUsage: The origin record identifies the vineyard as being in Champagne.

tuscany.definition: A region in central Italy with capital Florence.

napa-valley.definition: A region in California, United States, known internationally for vineyards and wine production.
napa-valley.exampleUsage: The geography display marks Napa Valley in northern California.

rioja.definition: A wine-growing region in northern Spain.

barossa-valley.definition: A region in South Australia known for vineyards and wine production.
barossa-valley.exampleUsage: The map shows Barossa Valley in South Australia.

mendoza.definition: A province and wine-growing region in western Argentina.

douro-valley.definition: In this wine-region context, the Portuguese valley associated with Port and other wines.
douro-valley.exampleUsage: The Douro Valley follows the Douro River through a steep landscape.

mosel.definition: A German wine-growing region along the Moselle River and nearby tributaries.
mosel.exampleUsage: The map traces the Mosel wine region along the river valley.

corkscrew.definition: A tool with a spiral metal point used to remove a cork from a bottle.
